question.problem:
$$
v=[\begin{aligned}a \\ b \\ c\end{aligned}],\,A=[\begin{aligned}2 & 0 & 0 \\ -3 & 3 & -3 \\ -1 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]
$$

The vector $v$ and the matrix $A$ are given above. 
If $v$ is an eigenvector of $A$ that corresponds to the eigenvalue $\lambda =1,$ then what is the value of $\frac{b}{c}?$
question.worked_solution:
To compute the eigenvectors of a matrix, we need to find non-zero solutions of the matrix equation 

$$
(A-\lambda I)\text{x}=0.
$$

 

In our case, we have $\lambda =1.$ So, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}A-\lambda I & =[\begin{aligned}2 & 0 & 0 \\ -3 & 3 & -3 \\ -1 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]-1[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ -3 & 2 & -3 \\ -1 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

To find the eigenvectors, we have to solve the corresponding homogeneous system of linear equations:

$$
\{\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}=0 \\ -3{x}_{1}+2{x}_{2}-3{x}_{3}=0 \\ -{x}_{1}=0\end{aligned}
$$

So, we row-reduce the augmented matrix $M$ to row echelon form using Gaussian elimination, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 & 0 \\ -3 & 2 & -3 & 0 \\ -1 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}] &  & \begin{aligned}{R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+3{R}_{1} \\ {R}_{3}:={R}_{3}+{R}_{1}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 2 & -3 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

In the reduced matrix above, there are two pivot columns (the $1$st and the $2$nd one). Thus, ${x}_{3}$ is a free variable. From the first equation, we obtain ${x}_{1}=0.$ From the second equation, we get ${x}_{2}=\frac{3}{2}{x}_{3}.$ Therefore, the general solution is

$$
[\begin{aligned}0 \\ \frac{3}{2}{x}_{3} \\ {x}_{3}\end{aligned}],\,{x}_{3}\in R.
$$

Setting, for instance, ${x}_{3}=2,$ we get the following eigenvector:

$$
v=[\begin{aligned}a \\ b \\ c\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 3 \\ 2\end{aligned}]
$$

Finally, $\frac{b}{c}=\frac{3}{2}.$
